problems.title: Distribute identical chocolates
problems.question: Distribute 12 identical chocolates to 5 distinct children, at least one each. How many ways?
problems.idea: Reserve one for each child first.
formulas: Positive integer solutions of x₁+…+x₅=12: C(11,4).
steps: After reserving 5, distribute 7 freely among 5 children.
Stars and bars gives C(7+5-1,5-1)=C(11,4)=330.

problems.title: Increasing digits need no permutation factor
problems.question: How many four-digit numbers have every digit greater than the preceding one?
problems.idea: Choose the digits; their order is forced.
steps: Zero cannot appear because it would have to be the first digit.
Choose any four of 1,…,9 and put them in increasing order.
This gives C(9,4)=126.

problems.title: Use the complement of repeated colours
problems.question: A box has 2 white,3 green,5 red balls. Three are selected uniformly without replacement. Find the probability that at least two share a colour.
problems.idea: The complement has exactly one of each colour.
steps: There are 120 equally likely three-ball subsets.
Exactly 30 contain all three colours.
The required probability is 1-30/120=3/4.

problems.title: Inclusion and exclusion for two events
problems.question: P(A)=0.7,P(B)=0.4,P(A∪B)=0.9. Find P(A∩B).
problems.idea: The overlap was counted twice when adding probabilities.
steps: Substitute to obtain 0.7+0.4-0.9=0.2.

problems.title: A three-dimensional dot product
problems.question: Find the cosine between m=(1,-1,1) and n=(1,2,-1).
problems.idea: Divide the dot product by the product of lengths.
steps: The dot product is 1-2-1=-2.
The lengths are √3 and √6.
The cosine is -2/√18=-√2/3.

problems.title: Two equivalent printed choices
problems.question: What necessarily follows from |a-b|=|a+b|?
problems.idea: Expand the squared lengths.
steps: Equality implies a·b=0.
For nonzero a,b, this is equivalent to a⊥b.
problems.answer: a·b=0, and nonzero vectors are perpendicular.
problems.note: Both the perpendicularity choice and zero-dot-product choice are valid for nonzero vectors. With zero vectors, the dot-product conclusion is still precise.

problems.title: A third component contributes zero
problems.question: For which a do m=(x,a,0),n=(x-a,1,a-2) form an acute angle for every real x?
problems.idea: Their dot product is a quadratic in x.
steps: The minimum is a-a²/4.
It must be strictly positive, so a(4-a)>0.
Thus 0<a<4; these values also ensure m,n are nonzero.

problems.title: The minus sign changes the cross term
problems.question: |a|=2,|b|=1 and their angle is 120°. Find |2a-3b|.
problems.idea: First calculate a·b.
steps: The squared length is 16+9+12=37.

problems.title: Two box vectors
problems.question: A rectangular box has AB=1,AD=2,AA₁=3. Find the cosine between AC and B₁D as directed vectors.
problems.idea: Use coordinates along the box edges.
steps: The dot product is -1+4=3.
The lengths are √5 and √14.

problems.title: A point one quarter along a segment
problems.question: N=(-1,3,-2),K=(1,-3,4),NM:MK=1:3. Find |OM|.
problems.idea: M lies one quarter of the way from N to K.
steps: Its distance to the origin is √(1/4+9/4+1/4)=√11/2.

problems.title: Probability as a square-area ratio
problems.question: Two independent uniform numbers are chosen from [-2,4]. Find the probability their squares sum to more than 4.
problems.idea: The complement is a radius-2 disk in the sampling square.
steps: The square has side 6 and area 36.
The whole disk x²+y²≤4 lies inside it and has area 4π.

problems.title: Compare a diagonal section with a side face
problems.question: A regular square-pyramid frustum has diagonal-section area equal to one lateral face area. Find the tangent of its base dihedral angle.
problems.idea: The shared sum of base sides cancels.
formulas: Let base sides A>B, height h,d=(A-B)/2 and slant height l=√(h²+d²).
steps: The diagonal section has bases √2A,√2B and height h, hence area (A+B)√2h/2.
A lateral face has area (A+B)l/2. Equality gives l=√2h.
Then h²+d²=2h², so d=h. The base dihedral tangent is h/d=1.

problems.title: A tetrahedron cut parallel to a lateral face
problems.question: In a regular tetrahedron a plane through the midpoint of its altitude, parallel to a lateral face, cuts off a smaller tetrahedron. Find the ratio of their total surface areas.
problems.idea: Find the position relative to the vertex opposite that lateral face.
formulas: For a tetrahedron, a plane parallel to a face gives similar tetrahedra; surface ratio=scale².
steps: Let S be the apex and O the centroid of base ABC. The midpoint T of SO has weights S:1/2,A:1/6,B:1/6,C:1/6.
Choose lateral face SAB, opposite C. The plane through T parallel to SAB is at one sixth of the altitude from that face toward C.
The small tetrahedron at C therefore has linear scale 5/6.
Its surface ratio is (5/6)²=25/36.

problems.title: Sine of a line-to-face angle
problems.question: A regular triangular prism has base side 6 and height 3. K is the midpoint of AC. Find the sine of the angle between B₁K and face BB₁C₁C.
problems.idea: Use perpendicular distance from K to that face.
steps: In the base, K is halfway up the altitude from A to BC, so its distance to BC is 3√3/2.
BK is a median of the equilateral base, length 3√3. Thus B₁K=√(27+9)=6.

problems.title: Square only after checking nonnegativity
problems.question: Solve |x|+1<√(5-x²).
problems.idea: Both sides are nonnegative on the square-root domain.
steps: Thus 0≤t<1, which automatically satisfies the original square-root domain.

problems.title: Prove there is exactly one positive-root input
problems.question: How many real solutions has x²-x-√x-2=0?
problems.idea: Use t=√x≥0 and compare increasing and decreasing functions.
steps: t=0 does not solve the equation.
On t>0 the left side t² strictly increases and the right side strictly decreases, so there is at most one intersection.
The original t-polynomial is negative at t=1 and positive at t=2. Continuity gives one intersection between them.

problems.title: Coplanarity is a zero scalar triple product
problems.question: Find m so a=(1,-1,3),b=(2,0,3),c=(4,-6,m) are coplanar.
problems.idea: Take the cross product of the first two vectors.
steps: The scalar product is -12-18+2m.
Set it to zero to get 2m=30.

problems.title: Two square roots lead to an absolute cosine
problems.question: Solve √(1+sinx)+√(1-sinx)=√3.
problems.idea: Both sides are nonnegative, so squaring is reversible.
steps: Thus |cosx|=1/2.
All such inputs satisfy the squared equation and hence the original nonnegative equation.

problems.title: Add the rational exponents
problems.question: Simplify ∛(⁵√a·⁴√(a³))·⁵√(¹²√(a¹¹)).
problems.idea: Even roots require a≥0.
steps: The first exponent is 19/60 and the second is 11/60.
Their sum is 30/60=1/2. The expression is also zero at a=0.

problems.title: Find all rational binomial terms
problems.question: Find the smallest rational term of (⁶√3+⁴√3)¹⁷.
problems.idea: Track the power of 3 in each term.
steps: For 0≤k≤17 the exponent is an integer only at k=2 and k=14.
The corresponding terms are 27C(17,2)=3672 and 81C(17,14)=55080.
The smaller is the first.

problems.title: Arithmetic progression of binomial coefficients
problems.question: For which n are the coefficients of terms 2,3,4 in (a+b)ⁿ in arithmetic progression?
problems.idea: Their middle coefficient must be the average.
steps: Substitute the factorial formulas and divide by n: n-1=1+(n-1)(n-2)/6.
Rearrange to (n-2)(n-7)=0.
Since the fourth term must exist, n=2 is excluded.

problems.title: A constant binomial term
problems.question: Find the term independent of x in (x+1/x²)¹².
problems.idea: Set its total exponent to zero.
steps: The exponent is zero at k=4.
The constant term is C(12,4)=495.

problems.title: The triangle inequality in space
problems.question: Minimize √((x-1)²+y²+(z+1)²)+√(x²+(y+2)²+(z-1)²).
problems.idea: Interpret the two radicals as distances from a moving point.
steps: Equality holds whenever P=(x,y,z) lies on segment AB.

problems.title: Count multiples of the least common multiple
problems.question: How many three-digit integers are multiples of 8,12 and 18?
problems.idea: They must be multiples of lcm(8,12,18).
steps: The integer quotients are 13 and 1.
Thus there are 13-1=12 multiples, from 144 through 936.

problems.title: Check whether the inequalities enclose a finite figure
problems.question: Find the perimeter of the region y≤|5x|-2, y≥-|5x|+8.
problems.idea: First determine which x allow the lower bound to be below the upper bound.
steps: For every x≥1 or x≤-1 the allowed y lie between two diverging lines.
The region consists of two unbounded wedges, so its boundary contains infinite rays.
It has no finite perimeter.
problems.answer: No finite perimeter; the printed system defines an unbounded region.
problems.note: None of the finite listed values is valid for the displayed inequalities. Reversing both inequality signs would define a different, bounded problem.
